name: Karma Choeling Buddhist Monastery
tradition: Karma Kagyu (Tibetan Vajrayana), New Zealand seat of the 17th Karmapa
technique: Ngondro preliminary practices, pujas (Tara, Chenrezig), sitting meditation
teacherAccess: Resident Kagyu sangha and visiting lamas
about: Established in 1980 on 20 hectares of regenerating native bush north of Auckland, with a temple, eight stupas, and a 25-foot Buddha statue. Offers residential retreat huts for weekend practice retreats plus regular Sunday sitting and pujas -- a long-standing, land-based Tibetan Buddhist community. Pricing and food/work details are not published; direct enquiry is needed.
